## ANP (Agent Network Protocol) Recon Summary

### Protocol Overview
ANP is an open-source protocol for agent-to-agent communication, positioned as "the HTTP of the Agentic Web Era." It aims to build an open, secure, and efficient collaboration network for billions of intelligent agents.

### Architecture (3-Layer)
1. **Identity Layer**: W3C DID-based decentralized authentication, E2E encrypted communication
2. **Meta-Protocol Layer**: Dynamic protocol negotiation, auto-organizing agent networks
3. **Application Layer**: Semantic-based capability description, Agent Description Protocol (ADP)

### Key Capabilities
- **Decentralized agent discovery** via DID-based identity verification
- **Peer-to-peer communication** using JSON-LD graphs
- **Capability discovery & interoperability** - agents can expose and discover capabilities
- **Dynamic negotiation** - automatic organizing among agents

### Community/Discovery
- Main site: agent-network-protocol.com
- GitHub: github.com/agent-network-protocol/AgentNetworkProtocol
- Technical whitepaper: arxiv.org/abs/2508.00007

### Protocol Handshake
Based on the architecture, ANP uses:
- DID documents for identity verification
- JSON-LD graph-based capability descriptions
- Meta-protocol negotiation for establishing connections

### Notes
No "anp.ai" domain exists; the protocol is hosted at agent-network-protocol.com. ANP competes with MCP (Model Context Protocol), A2A (Agent-to-Agent), and ACP (Agent Communication Protocol).
